name: Micturition-Induced Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Reflex Epilepsy Diagnosis

criteria.description: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing epileptiform discharges during or immediately after micturition
Exclusion of other causes of seizures or syncope unrelated to micturition
Detailed clinical history supporting reflex epilepsy triggered by urination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of seizures triggered by micturition with supporting ictal EEG findings and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by EEG; video-EEG monitoring during micturition may aid confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Focal seizures involving motor cortex activation during urination

common.symptomName: Aura of urinary urgency preceding seizure
common.notes: Subjective sensation of urgency before seizure onset
searchTerms: feeling urgent need to pee before seizure
warning sign of needing to urinate before seizure

common.notes: Loss of bladder control during ictal event
searchTerms: loss of bladder control in seizure

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms such as pallor or sweating
searchTerms: autonomic symptoms like pale skin or sweating

occasional.notes: Temporary inability to void after seizure
searchTerms: temporary inability to urinate after seizure

occasional.notes: Brief muscle jerks triggered by urination

rare.notes: Prolonged seizure activity induced by urination
Transient mood or behavioral changes after seizures
Temporary weakness on one side of the body after seizure
searchTerms: temporary weakness on one side after seizure

laboratory: Routine blood tests typically normal; metabolic panel to exclude secondary causes
imaging: Brain MRI usually normal; may show subtle cortical dysplasia in some cases
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible familial cases reported
other: Video-EEG monitoring demonstrating seizure onset triggered by micturition

distinguishingFeatures: Seizures triggered by stimuli other than micturition such as photic or auditory stimuli
Transient loss of consciousness related to vasovagal syncope during or after urination without epileptiform EEG changes

redFlags: Prolonged postictal unconsciousness or status epilepticus
Neurological deficits persisting beyond typical postictal period
references: Panayiotopoulos CP. Reflex epilepsies and reflex seizures. In: Epilepsy: A Comprehensive Textbook. 2nd ed. 2008.
Kasteleijn-Nolst Trenité DG, et al. Micturition-induced seizures: a rare form of reflex epilepsy. Epileptic Disord. 2013;15(3):302-306.
